basis: Skin scars occur in 80-99%; CNS injury and limb hypoplasia in 30-79%. Ocular malformations also occur in 30-79%, omitted at cap in favor of disabling limb defects.

decisions.ocular: none: ocular malformations qualify at 30-79%, but are omitted under the four-axis cap, prioritizing characteristic disabling limb hypoplasia.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: limb hypoplasia occurs in 30-79% and causes permanent structural and functional impairment.

basis: Beta-cell failure defines PNDM. Neurologic HPO findings cluster in syndromic subsets; >=30% CNS injury across the umbrella is unestablished. Diabetic retinal and renal disease are separate.

decisions.neurologic: none: the 30-79% HPO annotations reflect syndromic presentations; established neurologic injury is not demonstrably >=30% across the PNDM umbrella.

basis: Severe Zellweger disease defines metabolic and CNS dysfunction; hepatic disease typically affects >30%; renal dysplasia reported in 1/1. Skeletal and sensory involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe neonatal CNS dysfunction is a defining feature of the Zellweger phenotype, supported by seizures, hypotonia and areflexia in 1/1.

basis: The definition specifies a midline lower-lip cleft, affecting an oral structure; mandibular clefting is not required or established as common.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: despite the name and skeletal ancestor, the specific definition establishes only a lower-lip cleft; mandibular involvement is variable and unquantified.

basis: Intellectual disability, early balding and patellar/acral abnormalities are defining features; hypogonadism causes endocrine dysfunction in 30-79%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: premature balding is a named, defining manifestation and occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadism occurs in 30-79%; the three primary slots prioritize the defining intellectual, hair and skeletal abnormalities.

basis: Developmental impairment, limb malformations and cleft palate occur in 80-99%; cataract, microphthalmia and coloboma occur in 30-79%. Cardiac involvement lacks a qualifying frequency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is a major structural manifestation, annotated in 80-99%; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining limb malformations include syndactyly, abnormal phalanges and camptodactyly, each annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Neurocutaneous DNA-repair disorder; retinopathy 11/14, cataract 8/14 and sensorineural hearing loss 2/2. Kyphosis 2/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: photosensitive, progeroid skin and subcutaneous abnormalities are defining Cockayne features; subcutaneous fat loss is reported in 3/3.

basis: Intellectual disability, congenital ocular defects and hypogonadism characterize the syndrome; muscle hypoplasia/atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia, microcornea and cataract are characteristic structural abnormalities in the definition; cataract is annotated in 30-79%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypogenitalism is a defining manifestation, with hypogonadism explicitly annotated in 30-79%, supporting endocrine dysfunction.

basis: The metabolic umbrella includes mild forms without CNS injury. Severe untreated forms damage the brain, but established neurologic injury in >=30% across the full group is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurologic injury depends on biochemical severity and treatment; a >=30% frequency across the entire umbrella, including mild hyperphenylalaninemia, is not established.

basis: Hepatocerebral mitochondrial depletion defines metabolic, hepatic and neurologic disease. Retinopathy 2/2, hearing loss 1/1 and tubulopathy 1/1 do not establish >=30% disease-wide prevalence.

decisions.ocular: none: retinopathy in 2/2 selected reported patients does not establish >=30% prevalence across MPV17-related hepatocerebral disease; ocular disease is not a defining criterion.
